_meta.purpose: THE GOLDEN CONTROL SCHEMA — the canonical shape every SGS inspector control must have, expressed as DATA so one file drives enforcement (inspector-scan) and, later, generation. Answers 'does this control match its canonical shape?', not merely 'does a control exist?'.
_meta.source: Spec 35 PART O (the control-type contract) + Bean rulings 2026-08-19. Every figure below was produced by running a command against the tree on 2026-08-19; none is inherited from prose.
_meta.notEncoded: NONE of Part O's 14 contracts remain unencoded as of 2026-08-19 (this session added 13 rows — the 12 requested types + typography, which has no Part O contract of its own but is MANDATORY per plugins/sgs-blocks/CLAUDE.md R-22-13 — PLUS a 14th, 'link', which the task brief that produced this batch claimed was already done. It was NOT: this file's controls{} held only 'colour' at session start, and the OLD version of this exact notEncoded string listed link among the 12 still missing. Corrected here rather than left silently wrong; the pre-existing 'colour' row is the only one genuinely unchanged this session). The earlier objection recorded here — 'a schema covering 13 types on day one is 12 untested claims' — is DELIBERATELY OVERRIDDEN this session, on Bean's explicit instruction, because every added row now carries the command that produced each figure it states (measured2026_08_19 blocks throughout controls.*), so a claim here is falsifiable by re-running the cited command, not asserted from memory. Where a figure could not be independently re-measured this session (most Spec 35 spec-cited scope/conformance numbers, which require the out-of-repo DB this file's own whyRosterNotDb note already explains this repo cannot reach), each row says so explicitly rather than presenting a spec citation as a fresh measurement. CORRECTION recorded here (2026-08-19): the task briefing that produced this batch described 'plugins/sgs-blocks/scripts/inspector-scan/core/golden.js — the shared engine that consumes these rows' with a docblock stating 'a new control type is a schema row rather than new code'. THAT FILE DOES NOT EXIST. The only file that currently reads golden-controls.json is inspector-scan/rules/31-golden-colour-control.js, which is COLOUR-SPECIFIC hand-written logic, not a generic schema-driven engine. None of the 12 new rows in this file are enforced by any running rule yet — they are schema-only, ready for a future generic engine (or 12 future colour-31-style per-type rule files) to consume. Do not assume any of these rows are gating anything until a rule file that reads them exists.

stateVocabulary.source: THIS FILE. Corrected 2026-08-19 — an earlier draft deferred to scripts/consistency/cluster-member-sets.json -> states and called it the single source. IT IS NOT: every consumer of that file (check-element-manifest-conformance.js, check-cluster-coverage.py, placement-reach.py, extract-signatures.py) reads only its `clusters` and `order` keys. Its `states` block has ZERO readers — documentation sitting inside a data file, which is not a source of truth because nothing would notice it drifting.

current.note: Unifies the tabs case AND the nav case in one state. RENAMED from `selected` 2026-08-19 (D676 ruled it, D678 landed it) — code layer, classifier, 4 block.json manifests, the derived cache, and a /sgs-update reseed. Live DB verified: current 13, selected 0.

scrolled.why: Structurally identical to `current`: a class toggled at RUNTIME by view.js on the header element, painted by CSS in sgs/site-header/render.php. Not notional — the mechanism shipped long before the state was named, as the transparent-until-scrolled behaviour. Naming it lets the header background be ONE two-swatch colour row (at rest / once scrolled) instead of two single-state rows, which is both simpler for the client and what the 2-state minimum asks for.
scrolled.dbRowsNote: MEASURED 0 on 2026-08-19 (live query: NULL 2787, hover 115, current 13). It is 0 because css_state is DERIVED and the reseed that would populate it has NOT been run — a /sgs-update reseed is a SHARED-DB action and another session is live on this repo. Expect 2 after that reseed (site-header backgroundColourScrolled + textColourScrolled). Re-measure rather than trusting this line.

notional.why: Defined in cluster-member-sets.json's unread `states` block; ZERO rows in block_attributes.css_state (measured 2026-08-19: only NULL 2311, hover 113, selected 16). Treat as aspirational, never as an existing constraint.

stateVocabulary.renameResolved: DONE 2026-08-19. `selected` -> `current`. The original argument for `current` was WEAK (it claimed `active` would collide with a `pressed` state; `pressed` exists only in cluster-member-sets.json's unread block with zero DB rows). The decisive reasons were that `:active` is a real CSS pseudo-class we may still want, and `current` matches `aria-current` — the selector breadcrumbs already emits. Cost was a 9-step derived-column migration ending in a shared-DB reseed, since css_state is DERIVED and a direct UPDATE would be undone by the next reseed.

_meta.regenerate: HAND-MAINTAINED. Unlike roster.json this is a contract, not a derivation — it states what SHOULD be true, so it cannot be generated from the tree it governs.

colour.specRef: .claude/specs/35-BLOCK-INSPECTOR-UX-STANDARD.md PART O §1 (canonical) + §1 field 9 (the state + shape rule)

recipes._note: Source: .claude/plans/2026-08-22-colour-control-bundles-BRIEF.md 'The five members of the colour-control family' table (Bean-ruled 2026-08-22). This is the SINGLE contract both the rule-31 detector and every migration agent read for 'what does a conformant row/control look like' — so two agents cannot interpret the recipe differently. Only 0-rule-31-findings-for-that-row is CHECKABLE (enforced by a rule); rowShape/livesAs here are migration GUIDANCE, not gates (see phase-colour-conformance.md P-6).

text.rowShape: states[] + per-state gradient, plus gradientCapable: true (needs background-clip:text)

border.helperAdoption: The row-builder helper src/components/colour-variants/borderRow.js WAS DELETED at commit dd2989ec2 and is NOT exported from src/components/index.js. This entry previously described it as a live file with zero adopters, which was false. Border colour is owned by SgsBorderControl (44 adopters), not by a colour row. colour-codemod/adopt.js refuses border rows with REFUSED:border-helper-missing rather than emitting a call to a deleted module, and its self-test asserts every name it can emit is exported from the barrel. Fill and text siblings (fillRow.js, textRow.js) DO exist and ARE adopted. Re-verified 2026-09-03.

overlay.livesAs: SIBLING control (in BackgroundPanel) — NOT a SgsColourPanel row (Bean-ruled 2026-08-22: 'still a variation of the colour control which makes it a sibling control')
overlay.paintHelper: sgs_overlay_decls() — fill applied to a scrim element
overlay.rowShape: same states[] shape as the panel rows, alpha OFF, own row presentation + help text
overlay.requiredSiblings: {attr}Gradient per state, plus backgroundOverlayOpacity{,Tablet,Mobile} and backgroundOverlayBlendMode

shadow.paintHelper: colour only — no gradient helper exists BY DESIGN (box-shadow takes a colour; a gradient there is invalid CSS)
shadow.rowShape: states[], NO gradient path — gradient-EXEMPT by mechanism, not by per-block declaration

panel.adoption: 65 of 83 blocks (re-measured 2026-08-30; the earlier '60 of 83' figure was stale — command: grep -l "<SgsColourPanel" plugins/sgs-blocks/src/blocks/*/edit.js | wc -l)
panel.note: The grouped panel. Named in Part O §1 field 1 (2026-08-19) and its placement/omission rule is now field 9e/9f (added 2026-08-30) — see controls.colour.placement below for the machine-readable form.

row.api: states={[{ key, label, value, onChange, linked?, gradientValue?, onGradientChange? }]}
row.⚠ notTheSpecsNamedComponent: Part O §6 STATE/HOVER names StateToggleControl as the canonical state component and calls it 'verified adoptable today' with a live nav-menu mount. FALSE, and Spec 35:736 says so itself: StateToggleControl has 0 JSX mounts across src/blocks (measured 2026-08-19); its only references are two comments recording where it USED to live (brand-strip/edit.js:316, nav-menu/edit.js:463) plus its own file. The working mechanism is SgsColourPanel rows -> DesignTokenPicker states, which is what this schema encodes.
row.note: Renders a popover; a TabPanel appears when states.length > 1 (DesignTokenPicker.js:205, :400-416); a per-state Solid/Gradient ToggleGroupControl appears when the state carries onGradientChange (:289-317). Part O §1 field 9's '⚠ NOT YET BUILT — no state axis and no popover' is STALE as of 2026-08-19: all three exist.

textGradientRow.independentlySufficientWhy: Reached ONLY through a SgsColourPanel row declaring gradientCapable:true, never mounted directly — so reaching it proves the panel is already there and it can never independently prove conformance.
textGradientRow.whenToUse: TEXT gradients only — they need background-clip:text, a genuinely different CSS mechanism from a background/border gradient.
textGradientRow.reachedVia: a SgsColourPanel row declaring gradientCapable: true. Never mounted directly.

wholeBlockOverlay.independentlySufficientWhy: Single-state by construction, a whole-block overlay rather than the block's colour panel. sgs/site-footer reaches it via BackgroundPanel while still having NO SgsColourPanel — scoring that CONFORMANT hid a real violation (measured 2026-08-20).
wholeBlockOverlay.constraint: NO LONGER SINGLE-STATE (corrected 2026-08-22, D738). It now takes a normal + hover pair and renders them as TABS INSIDE ONE POPOVER via DesignTokenPicker's states array, so a row needing hover CAN use it. The previous text was accurate when written and was load-bearing: it predicted, in advance, the exact failure that then happened — a dispatch scoped to BackgroundPanel.js could not lift the constraint, so hover shipped as a SECOND ROW instead of a tab. Hover is emitted only when the caller's attrNames carries solidHover/gradientHover, so callers passing a custom map without them (the two shape-divider rows, hero media/content backgrounds) keep one state and no tabs. ⛔ Build its states as LITERAL array entries, never a .map() over a spec list: rule 31 resolves the state count STATICALLY and cannot evaluate a runtime predicate. A first fix used .filter().map(), rendered both states correctly, and made the rule report 'carries 1 state' — the code improved while the gate went blind, which is worse than the honest finding it replaced.

bannedLookalikes._note: ALL FOUR ARE AT ZERO LIVE INSTANCES as of 2026-08-19 (verified in src/blocks/*/edit.js). These are REGRESSION GUARDS, not a backlog. Part O §1's named violator sgs/star-rating was fixed — it now mounts SgsColourPanel (star-rating/edit.js:134), so §1 field 6's '49/50 conform, star-rating violates' is stale.

patterns.shape: <TextControl type="color" />
patterns.why: a raw browser colour input bypasses the theme token palette entirely

bannedLookalikes.matchRule: EXACT JSX-identifier match via Set membership, never substring. `MyColorPaletteButton` tokenises to a different identifier and must not flag. Any tag regex uses \b — multi-line JSX puts `<Component` at end-of-line and `[\s/>]` returns a false absence.

nativeUi._note: Bean's addition 2026-08-19: core's own colour UI is a fingerprint to detect and replace. It does NOT arrive via JSX — there are ZERO raw ColorPalette/PanelColorSettings mounts in any of the 83 edit.js files. It arrives through block.json supports.color, from which WordPress renders its own panel in the Styles tab.
nativeUi.detectVia: block.json supports.color — any sub-flag set true
nativeUi.conformantShape: declared with every sub-flag false (keeps __experimentalSkipSerialization while suppressing core's UI)
nativeUi.sequencingConstraint: Part O Cross-cutting A: the three-tab bar lands AFTER native-supports retirement, because while a block declares native color, core renders its own Styles tab regardless of what SGS does. DETECT NOW; retire per that existing plan, never ad hoc.
nativeUi.doNotDuplicate: Rule 24 (24-raw-canonical-component) already gates the JSX half. It never opens block.json, so this fingerprint does not overlap it.

states.minimumMeans: normal + hover. Bean ruling 2026-08-19: every colour row carries at least two states by default.

derivation.rule: A row's required state set = ['normal'] + the states DECLARED on its element in block.json supports.sgs.elements.<el>.states.
derivation.why: This needs no new vocabulary and no hardcoded 'is this a nav block' roster — the manifest already declares states per element, and Spec 35 FR-35-5 requires states be DECLARED, never parsed from attribute names (tabActiveTextColour renders as [aria-selected="true"], NOT :active; pauseOnHover/grayscaleHover contain 'Hover' but are booleans).

shapeRule.9a: ONE CONTROL SHAPE EVERYWHERE — a thin row carrying its swatches, showing how many states are pickable, picker in a popover.
shapeRule.9b: STATES LIVE INSIDE THE CONTROL — a tab toggle within the popover; never sibling controls, never a second panel.
shapeRule.9c: A COLOUR IS NEVER AN OPTIONAL ToolsPanelItem — not behind the '+' menu, not hideable per instance.

referenceImplementations.twoState: sgs/button — edit.js:381-470, one SgsColourPanel, 5 rows, all 2-state, 3 of 5 gradient-capable. The best 2-state+gradient example in the tree.
referenceImplementations.threeState: sgs/tabs — edit.js:176-199, tab-bg with normal/hover/active. The ONLY 3-state colour row in the entire library (measured 2026-08-19).

exemption.shape: block.json supports.sgs.colourExemptions.<rowKey> = { "rule": "states", "reason": "<why this element has no hover state>" }
exemption.whenValid: ONLY when the row paints an element that CANNOT be hovered — a drawer panel, a section background, body text. A hover state there would be a control the client can set and never see.
exemption.neverValid: NEVER to record that a block has not wired hover yet. Bean's ruling 2026-08-22: an exemption may not remove a capability the block already has. sgs/button's text row is the named case — it declares colourText AND colourTextHover and had a real hover text colour under WP-native colour support; it must never become states-exempt.
exemption.enforcedStructurally: The neverValid clause is NOT left to the prose. rule 31 REFUSES a states exemption whenever the block already declares a matching `<attr>Hover` attribute: if that attribute exists, the element demonstrably can carry a hover state, so the row is unwired rather than un-hoverable. A boilerplate reason is refused separately by hasRealReason().
exemption.negativeControls: Proven three ways 2026-08-22 on sgs/whatsapp-cta: real reason + no hover attr -> ALLOWED (finding suppressed); same reason + a declared labelColourHover -> REFUSED; boilerplate reason -> REFUSED.

gradient.requiredMeans: Bean ruling 2026-08-19: UNIVERSAL, WITH DECLARED EXEMPTIONS. Every colour row must offer a gradient path unless its block.json declares an exemption with a reason. An absent gradient is a finding; a justified one is data.

mechanisms.how: a per-state gradient toggle inside DesignTokenPicker — the state carries gradientValue + onGradientChange, backed by a sibling {attr}Gradient string attribute
GradientCapableColourControl via a row declaring gradientCapable: true — text gradients need background-clip:text

<rowKey>.reason: <why this row has no valid gradient form>

exemption.expectedFirstExemption: shadow colour — a box-shadow colour has no gradient form; a gradient control there would produce invalid CSS
exemption.rule: A reason string is REQUIRED and must not be boilerplate. An exemption without a real reason is itself a finding — same discipline as inspector-scan baselines (core/baseline.js hasRealReason).

gradient.blockedOnNothing: The gradient picker crashed every block until 2026-08-19 (fixed in daeec438 + 3fa0ebbd). The parked universal rollout is P-GRADIENT-UNIVERSAL-ROLLOUT.
gradient.⚠ unverifiedSurface: Because the crash masked it, NO gradient row in the library has ever been seen working. Treat 'it has a gradient toggle' as UNPROVEN until looked at in the live editor.

exemptByMechanism.case: A TEXT row whose element ALSO paints a background.
exemptByMechanism.why: A text gradient is background-image plus background-clip:text, and background-clip clips the element's WHOLE background painting area to the glyph shapes — background-COLOUR included. On an element carrying its own background, a gradient would clip that fill to the letters and destroy it.
exemptByMechanism.statedOnce: Read from the element manifest by rule 31 (textSharesElementWithBackground): an element whose attrMap maps both a css:color* and a css:background* member IS the shared element. No block roster is hardcoded and no per-block entry has to be written and kept honest — the same shape as the shadow exemption (S-3).
exemptByMechanism.consequence: sgs/button's per-block colourExemptions.text entry was REMOVED 2026-08-22: with the mechanism stating the fact, that entry was a second owner, and if the two ever disagreed the per-block one would silently win. Verified neutral — removing it left rule 31 at 355 with zero sgs/button findings.
exemptByMechanism.notALimitOfCSS: This is a DOM-shape constraint, not a CSS law. An element with an inner text node can carry both. sgs/button is exempt because D288 makes the <a> itself the block root, leaving no inner element; sgs/nav-drawer is NOT exempt because it paints text on .sgs-nav-drawer__body while the background sits on the dialog root.

qualifiesWhen._why: scope.eligible is DESCRIPTIVE and therefore SELF-FULFILLING: build-roster.py:106 computes surfaces.colour as `"color" in supports or an attribute named colour/color`, i.e. it is true exactly when the block ALREADY has colour. A block with none is excluded from this contract and can never be reported as MISSING a colour panel — only blocks that have some colour and got the shape wrong are visible. This predicate answers the other question: SHOULD this block have one? Added 2026-08-19.
qualifiesWhen._engineIsGeneric_predicateIsPerFamily: The engine evaluating this is shared; the evidence is not. Colour qualifies on painted surfaces; typography on rendered text; spacing on a box element; layout on multiple children; shadow on a card-like surface; link on an <a> or URL attribute. Each control type declares its own qualifiesWhen here rather than the engine growing a branch per family.

paintsOwnSurface.match: a CSS declaration of background, background-color, border-color or color
paintsOwnSurface.cssPropertiesNote: Added 2026-08-20. Bare CSS property names, matched literally against the block's own style.css by survey-golden-conformance.js's ownPaintRegex(). Until this field existed colour was the ONLY styling type still resolving through that function's hardcoded-regex fallback — backwards for the type that is meant to be the reference implementation for the other twelve. ⛔ The fallback's `[^-\w]` guard is NOT optional and was reproduced as a `(?<![-\w])` lookbehind in the same commit BEFORE this field was added: without it a bare `color` alternative also matches inside `--brand-color:` and `-webkit-text-fill-color:`, and qualifiesFor() reads the MATCH COUNT rather than a boolean, so the inflation would propagate into the census. Verified by the gate that governs this change: survey-golden-conformance.js --json is byte-identical before and after, diffed against .claude/reports/2026-08-20-colour-golden-raw/golden-conformance.json.
paintsOwnSurface.means: there is a surface for a colour control to govern

paintedByAncestor._note: ⚠ MEASURED 2026-08-19, and it changes WHERE the control belongs, not whether it exists. Every sgs/form-field-* block declares 4 elements (label/input/help/error) and paints ZERO of them; sgs/form paints all 52. So the field blocks qualify for colour COLLECTIVELY, and the control belongs on the ANCESTOR with children inheriting — the group-default pattern sgs/multi-button already proves (--sgs-mb-btn-*-default, D640). A predicate that only looked at the block's own stylesheet would wrongly report 13 form blocks as NOT-APPLICABLE.
paintedByAncestor.source: declared supports.sgs.elements with zero own paint declarations
paintedByAncestor.means: qualifies, but the control's home is the ancestor that paints it

featureParity.means: an SGS block replacing a core block must meet or exceed it (standing rule sgs-block-feature-parity-with-replaced-core), so if the replaced core block has colour supports this one qualifies

qualifiesWhen.verdicts: QUALIFIES + has a canonical panel = CONFORMANT. QUALIFIES + none = MISSING (real work). Does NOT qualify = NOT-APPLICABLE (not a backlog item, and must never be counted as one).

scope.whyRosterNotDb: roster.json is in-repo, DB-derived, regenerated in prebuild and staleness-gated. The canonical DB lives OUTSIDE the repo and two 0-byte decoys sit inside it — a relative resolve lands on an empty file and passes clean forever.
scope.nullSurfacesRule: A block on disk but ABSENT from roster.json gets surfaces: null (core/roster.js:170,182), and reading .colour off it throws. An advisory rule that throws is SKIPPED, not failed (run.js:189-201) — it goes dark and green. Treat null surfaces as UNKNOWN, NOT CLEAN: emit an informational finding. Self-test cannot catch this (fixtures always get {}, never null).

placement._note: Added 2026-08-30. Answers 'where does this control go?', not 'what shape is it?' (that half is controls.colour.states.shapeRule above). specRef: .claude/specs/35-BLOCK-INSPECTOR-UX-STANDARD.md PART O §1 fields 9e/9f.

onePanelPerBlock.rule: SgsColourPanel is mounted AT MOST ONCE per block. Every colour row that block declares — however many elements those rows belong to — renders inside that one panel instance.
onePanelPerBlock.measured2026_08_30: Verified across all 65 adopting blocks: 0 blocks mount it 0 times having imported it, 65 mount it exactly once, 0 mount it 2+ times.
onePanelPerBlock.command: for f in $(grep -l "<SgsColourPanel" plugins/sgs-blocks/src/blocks/*/edit.js); do grep -c "<SgsColourPanel" "$f"; done | sort | uniq -c

omissionNotDisabling.rule: A row that does not apply to the block's current variant/config is OMITTED from the `rows` array passed to SgsColourPanel — never rendered disabled, never CSS-hidden.
omissionNotDisabling.mechanism: SgsColourPanel.js:109 — `(rows || []).filter(Boolean)`. A falsy array entry (e.g. `condition && {...}`) drops silently before render.
omissionNotDisabling.referenceImplementation: sgs/icon-list, edit.js:328 — icon-colour row omitted unless the marker renders an icon/emoji glyph; border-colour row omitted unless a border style is selected. Cites D609 9c in its own inline comment.
omissionNotDisabling.relationToField9c: Extends field 9c ('a colour is never an optional ToolsPanelItem, never hideable behind a +') from an APPLICABLE-colour disclosure ban to an INAPPLICABLE-colour existence ban — the row must not be in the array at all, not merely undisclosed.

elementPanelException.why: The one purpose-built composite that renders a colour inside an ELEMENT's own panel instead of the shared SgsColourPanel — it pairs border colour with width/style/radius on shared popover lines (Spec 35 §14, D881).
elementPanelException.howItDiffers: SgsBorderControl owns its colour rendering internally. It does not call SgsColourPanel and does not use the rows={[...]} shape — so it neither competes with nor counts against the one-panel-per-block rule above.
elementPanelException.generalMechanismStatus: NOT BUILT. SgsColourPanel hardcodes its own InspectorControls group="styles" + PanelBody title="Colour" (SgsColourPanel.js:116-121), and zero blocks render a colour control directly inside an element panel outside SgsBorderControl. A second element-panel colour composite requires a design gate before any block adopts it — do not extend this pattern ad hoc per block.

canonical.path: (@wordpress/components — no local SGS file; the contract is the DECLARED block.json enum it's bound to, not a shared SGS wrapper)
canonical.nativeContract: REQUIRED: onChange (Job 1 extract-native-contracts.py, select-control.md). value/options are optional per the README but structurally load-bearing.
canonical.adoption: REACH 75 of 83 blocks (measured 2026-08-19, survey-control-reach.py) — direct 70, +5 via the conditional-visibility.js extension surface

alt.adoption: REACH 64 of 83 (measured 2026-08-19) — direct 7, +57 via the responsive-device-toggle.js extension surface (the GLOBAL device toggle, not a per-block enum mount)
alt.note: Spec 35 §3.1: 'short option sets' — no written threshold, so a rule cannot yet gate SelectControl-vs-ToggleGroupControl choice, only that the CHOSEN one's options match the declared enum.

canonical.note: No shared SGS wrapper component exists for this type (Spec 35 §3.1: 'no shared component'). The canonical SHAPE is: SelectControl/ToggleGroupControl options === the block.json declared enum, exactly.

bannedLookalikes._note: Spec 35 §3.3: (a) a shared aggregator (e.g. LayoutPanel) offering options OUTSIDE the consuming block's own declared enum; (b) a PHP-enforced closed set with NO block.json enum at all (free-text box, no validation). Neither is a JSX-identifier ban like colour's — this type's violation is a VALUE-SET mismatch, not a banned component.

patterns.shape: a shared control's hardcoded option list diverging from the consuming block's declared enum
patterns.why: Spec 35 §3.6 names 3 live defects on ONE shared control: sgs/testimonial-slider (enum full|split vs picker stack|flex|grid — ZERO overlap), sgs/post-grid (enum grid|list|masonry|carousel, only grid overlaps), sgs/feature-grid (render.php:131 hardcodes layout='grid' before calling the wrapper — the control is live, visible and inert)
patterns.liveInstances: 3 confirmed + 9 further blocks with kind="layout" and no enum at all + 13 attrs across 8 blocks PHP-enforced with no declared enum (spec-cited, not independently re-measured this session)

patterns.shape: PHP-enforced closed set with no block.json enum
patterns.why: free-text box accepting any string, no validation
patterns.liveInstances: 13 attrs / 8 blocks per Spec 35 §3.6 (spec-cited, not independently re-run this session)

bannedLookalikes.matchRule: This type's ban is a SET-DIFFERENCE check (rendered options vs declared enum), not a Set-membership JSX-identifier check like colour's bannedLookalikes.jsxComponents — recorded here so a future rule author does not force this type into colour's shape.

nativeUi._note: No core supports.* flag maps to an arbitrary enum (WP has no generic 'enum' supports capability) — this type has no native-UI competitor to detect.

shapeRule.rule1: value bound to the attr; options array's value set must equal the block.json declared enum SET EXACTLY (not a superset, not a subset)
shapeRule.rule2: a shared aggregator (LayoutPanel-style) must build its options FROM the consuming block's own enum, never a fixed list (Spec 35 §3.8, open Rule-7 design gate — NOT yet built)

exemption.declareAt: block.json supports.sgs — no dedicated exemption key exists yet for this type
exemption.shape: NOT YET DEFINED — Spec 35 §3 records no exemption mechanism; unlike colour's colourExemptions, an enum either has a declared block.json enum or it doesn't. Recorded as an open gap rather than invented.
exemption.rule: A future exemption key must still carry a non-boilerplate reason, per the same discipline as colour.

scope.eligible: roster.json has NO dedicated 'enum' surface flag (only styling/colour/link/media/animation exist) — scope instead comes from Spec 35 §3.5: 284 rows with a declared block.json enum; 1,372 string rows are the wider search space, not the violator count (spec-cited figures, not independently re-measured this session).
scope.rosterPath: scripts/consistency/roster.json (surfaces object does not cover this type — see nullSurfacesRule discipline in controls.colour.scope, same caveat applies)

toggleGroupControlReach.note: inflated by the global device toggle extension surface (57 of the 64) — the per-block enum-mount count is 7

canonical.wraps: UnitControl (@wordpress/components) with a REAL units array — never px-only
canonical.nativeContract: UnitControl README (unit-control.md) declares NO required props at all (all optional) — value/onChange/units are all 'Required: No'. The REQUIREDNESS is structural (SGS's own rule, not WordPress's): a units array with only px is a banned lookalike per §4.3, even though the native component doesn't enforce it.
canonical.adoption: REACH 51 of 83 blocks for UnitControl (measured 2026-08-19); ResponsiveControl itself REACH 64 of 83 (shared with the responsive-wrapper type below — it is the SAME primitive, this row is the length-specific USE of it)

altForObjectCascade.when: the attr family is object-typed ({desktop,tablet,mobile}) rather than flat scalar+Tablet+Mobile siblings — per Spec 35 §12's binding STORAGE-SHAPE pairing table

bannedLookalikes._note: Spec 35 §4.3, all three RESOLVED as of 2026-08-11 (D561) — 0 live violations. Kept as regression guards, exactly like colour's zero-instance set.

patterns.shape: raw-px RangeControl standing in for a length control
patterns.why: 0 live violations found (the only RangeControl hits in the shadow builder's sliders are correct, not a length-unit case)

patterns.shape: TextControl standing in for UnitControl
patterns.why: accepts invalid CSS, e.g. sgs/card-grid.cardRadius's old help text 'e.g. 8px' — FIXED 2026-08-11 (D561)

bannedLookalikes.matchRule: Same Set-membership discipline as colour: exact JSX identifier, never substring.

Scope is therefore UNRESOLVED for this type — recorded as an honest gap, not guessed.

canonical.supersessionNote: Bean ruled 2026-08-13: SgsLinkControl's INLINE mount is retired as the canonical shape (kept only as a legacy shim for repeater-item consumers not yet migrated). Root-caused core LinkControl's 350px floor overflowing a ~248px inline panel + staged settings toggles with no blur/close commit, by moving onto core's own designed home (a popover with a real Submit interaction, matching core/button).

knownStaleTrap_link_backlog.claim: Spec 35 §2.6 (dated 2026-08-13) names 7 blocks still on SgsLinkControl's inline mount: brand-strip, card-grid, form, pricing-table, social-icons, team-member, trust-bar.
knownStaleTrap_link_backlog.reMeasured2026_08_19: survey-control-mounts.py's ZERO MOUNTS ANYWHERE line reports SgsLinkControl at 0 mounts tree-wide — a DIFFERENT figure from the spec's 7-block backlog. Recorded as an open discrepancy, NOT resolved here: either the 7-block migration completed since the spec text was last edited, or (more likely, per the D523 repeater-item blind spot this same spec documents elsewhere) the survey script's per-file scan cannot see repeater-item mounts the same way it cannot see pricing-table's item editor. Do not trust either figure over the other without opening the 7 named files directly — flagged, not guessed.

shapeRule.rule1: LinkPopoverField requires label, value, onChange. Two value shapes: object {url, linkId, linkKind, linkTarget, rel, download} (default) or bare string (searchOnly).
shapeRule.rule2: targetMode ('enum' 4-value _self/_blank/_parent/_top, or 'boolean' open-in-new-tab) must match which shape the consumer's OWN schema declares — do not default to 'enum' for a boolean-typed schema attr, the exact 'flat value on an object attr' coercion-trap class of bug this file's own colour row and length-unit row both warn about elsewhere.
shapeRule.rule3: enableInternalResolution opts a consumer INTO linkId/linkKind render-time ID resolution, off by default (only sgs/button's render.php resolves them today per the spec's own text)

exemption.declareAt: N/A — Spec 35 §2 records no exemption mechanism.
